summary: Three new or revived citizenship-by-investment schemes have an official legal basis. Nauru (Act No. 15 of 2024; regulations from Oct 2024, restructured Jan 2026) is fully documented in the Gazette, but its only outcome figure is the IMF's AU$0.24 million revenue for FY2025. São Tomé and Príncipe (Decree-Law 07/2025, in force 1 Aug 2025) publishes only a promotional "more than 220 applications". Argentina has a legal basis (DNU 366/2025, Decreto 524/2025) and an agency but no published investment threshold, so it is not operating. Nauru's earlier 1998-2003 scheme is documented by its 1997 Act and an academic estimate. Sierra Leone and other reported plans could not be checked (see gaps).

sources.title: Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15 of 2024)
sources.covers: Founding Act of the 2024 programme: eligibility, Program Office, agents, contribution paid to the Treasury Fund, cancellation of citizenship.
sources.notes: Copy retrieved from the FAO FAOLEX database; the RONLAW (ronlaw.gov.nr) link for the same Act returns the database web app rather than the PDF to a direct download. Certified 20 August 2024 and in force on certification (s. 2). Later instruments cite a section 9(7) and section 31 that are not in this text, so the Act has been amended since; the amending Act was not found.

programs.name: Nauru (Naoero) Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program (NECRCP / ECRCP)
programs.notes: Set up by the Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Act 2024 (No. 15 of 2024, certified 20 Aug 2024); prices in Regulations SL 28 of 2024 (gazetted 30 Oct 2024). Unveiled at COP29 on 13 Nov 2024 and launched by the President in Singapore on 28 Nov 2024; the IMF gives 2025 as inception year. One route: a non-refundable contribution to the Treasury Fund, applications only through licensed agents, run by a Program Office based in Auckland and operated by a private firm. Prices were restructured on 29 Jan 2026 (USD 115,000 single applicant) and a temporary USD 90,000 discount applies to 31 Dec 2026. No official statistics on applications or grants are published; the IMF reports FY2025 revenue of AU$0.24 million and the authorities cite low take-up.

programs.name: Nauru Citizen Investor scheme (Nauruan Community Act 1956-1997, s. 5(6)-(9))
programs.notes: Created by the Nauruan Community Ordinance Amendment Act 1997 (No. 11 of 1997): citizenship for a person who made an investment "of such form and in such amount as determined by Cabinet", vetted by a Nauru Citizen Investment Board. Dates of operation (1998 to 2003), the about 1,000 sales and the end after concerns about passports used by suspected terrorists come from an academic report citing secondary work, not from official records.

programs.name: São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment or Donation Programme (Programa de Cidadania por Investimento ou Doação, PCID)
programs.notes: Legal basis: Nationality Law No. 7/2022 of 10 Mar 2022 (art. 10(2), art. 26) and Decree-Law No. 07/2025 (approved 10 May 2025, published and in force 1 Aug 2025), which creates the programme, the Citizenship by Investment and Donation Unit (UCID, under the Justice Minister) and the National Transformation Fund (FNT). One route: non-refundable contribution to the FNT after approval in principle (USD 90,000 single applicant). The Decree-Law requires quarterly reports to the Justice Minister, Public Prosecutor and National Assembly and an annual independent audit of the FNT; none were found published. The programme site claims more than 220 applications by 2 Mar 2026. A formal national launch conference was held in Oct 2025.

programs.name: Argentina citizenship by investment (Ley de Ciudadanía 346, art. 2 inc. 2, as amended by Decreto 366/2025)
programs.notes: Legal basis exists but no operating programme was found. Decree of necessity and urgency 366/2025 (28 May 2025) lets foreigners who make a "relevant investment" naturalise regardless of residence and creates the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión under the Ministry of Economy; Decreto 524/2025 sets the procedure; Ley 27802 (2026) settles tax residence of such citizens; the Agency got an executive director from 22 Apr 2026. The Ministry of Economy has to define what counts as a relevant investment: no such resolution was found in the Boletín Oficial up to 1 Oct 2026, so there are no published amounts. Whether Congress has reviewed or rejected the DNU was not checked.

gaps: Web search budget for the session ran out early in this pass, so the broad search for other announced schemes (Sierra Leone, other African and Pacific states) could not be done. No official or serious source was read for Sierra Leone, so it has no row or event. This is the biggest gap.

Nauru: no official statistics on applications, approvals, grants, nationality of applicants or contributions received. The Act requires a yearly list of grants to the Registrar (s. 10(3)) and an independent auditor (s. 14), but nothing is published. The only outturn is the IMF's AU$0.24 million for FY2025.
Nauru: the Act was amended (later instruments cite s. 9(7) and s. 31, which are not in the 2024 text), but the amending Act was not found. RONLAW is a web app that blocks direct PDF downloads.
Nauru: no official document gives the date applications opened. Industry reports say 1 January 2025; the IMF gives 2025 as inception year.
Nauru: national budget documents (FY2025/26, FY2026/27) were not checked for budgeted or actual citizenship revenue.

Nauru 1998-2003 scheme: the regulations, the Cabinet-set investment amount, the number of citizenships granted and the closure decision were not found in official sources. Only an academic estimate (about 1,000 sales, 8% of GDP) is recorded.

São Tomé and Príncipe: the Decree-Law copy is a gazette scan hosted by an industry site. No copy on a government site was found, nor the text of Nationality Law 7/2022. The quarterly reports (art. 21) and FNT audits (art. 7) the decree requires were not found. There are no approval, revenue or nationality figures, and no information on who the private managing entity (Entidade Gestora) is, if any.
São Tomé and Príncipe: the programme site says citizens get visa-free access to over 93 countries. No independent check was made, and no EU or UK reaction was found.

Argentina: whether Congress has reviewed or rejected DNU 366/2025, and whether any court challenge affects the citizenship articles, was not checked. No Ministry of Economy resolution defining a relevant investment was found in the Boletín Oficial (searched 1 May 2025-1 Oct 2026), so there are no terms and no applications.

Pacific: Solomon Islands (reported in 2020 as considering a scheme), Tonga, Kiribati, Tuvalu and Marshall Islands passport sales are covered only in the EUI report and were not researched. Papua New Guinea's 2016 constitutional amendment was not read.
